ask: Just a shell for an HR onboarding portal: nav with 6 sections, and only the 'First day checklist' page built properly. It's for a stakeholder walkthrough tomorrow morning.
notes: The person states the depth: a shell plus one page in full. A default of 'every module in full' goes against their words. The six section names are open and fair to draft as a default.
message:
Goal: a clickable HR onboarding portal shell with a 6-section nav, where only "First day checklist" is built properly, ready for tomorrow morning's stakeholder walkthrough.

Found:
- Scope: nav with 6 sections, one page built in full (from your message)
- Purpose: stakeholder walkthrough tomorrow morning (from your message)
- Lands in: `hr-onboarding-portal/index.html` in this folder, one file, local link only. The folder is empty, so nothing existing to build on.
- The 5 other sections are titled pages with a short line on what will go there (default; you asked for a shell)
- Browser found, so every click is checked in a real browser, not only page loads

Track: quick, because you asked for a shell with one page built.

Still open after reading your files: who uses the checklist, the names of the 5 other sections, what "built properly" covers, the look.

Done means:
- Nav shows 6 sections and each one opens
- First day checklist works: tick items, see progress
- Checklist has an empty and an all-done state
- Other 5 pages are titled, with no dead clicks
- Every link opens with no page error

About 30 minutes and 5 helper agents, within a budget of 120 minutes.

1. Who uses the checklist, and what one job do they come to do?
   Recommended: a new hire on their first day, ticking off what they must do, with the HR owner of each item shown.
   Why it matters: the persona decides what each checklist item says and who it points to.

2. What are the 6 section names?
   Recommended: Home, First day checklist, Documents, Training, Team and contacts, Benefits.
   Why it matters: the nav is the first thing stakeholders see.

3. What must the checklist page do for the walkthrough?
   Recommended: tick items, a progress bar, item detail with the owner and due time, and an all-done message.
   Why it matters: this is the one page built in full, so it sets the depth of the demo.

4. Do you have a logo, colours or fonts to use?
   Recommended: none, so the plain look: white page, dark text, one blue accent, initials instead of photos.
   Why it matters: stakeholders judge the look as much as the flow.

The full brief is in `loop-runs/product-build-loop-20261126-035045/brief.md`.

Reply with your answers, or just "go" to use the defaults.
